Meeting header
Date: 2027-02-27
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (CSM) -- Samantha Lee (Argosy), Ravi Patel (Argosy SRE), Nina Brooks (Argosy Head of AI), Tom Erickson (Argosy Legal)

Summary: quick follow-up from last week's escalation; go over root cause, patch status, mitigations, and next steps. Customer concerned about recurring latency spikes and automated fallback behavior during the incident.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you all making time, uh this is Maya from Redwood, i'm joined by diego and priya. how's everyone doing over there?
[00:12] Samantha: good, thanks, still dealing with a few internal postmortem steps but wanted to align on the patch and the rollback plan.
[00:22] Diego: yeah quick update from our side: we pushed a candidate hotfix for the KV cache eviction race and tightened the autoscaler backoff windows. we ran internal stress tests that look promising but want you to validate on your traffic profile.
[00:36] Ravi: thanks, can you clarify the root cause again? there was some mention of cache invalidation plus a thrash in autoscaling?
[00:45] Maya: sure, high-level: during the incident the runtime hit an edge case where a race in the prefix/KV cache eviction allowed stale keys to be referenced; that caused increased tail latency as the engine retried certain requests and then the autoscaler observed sudden CPU spikes and started provisioning nodes, which overshot and then scaled down repeatedly — so thrash. combination of KV race + aggressive autoscaler backoff was the amplifier.
[01:15] Nina: and that retried requests returned partial responses sometimes which caused downstream app errors, yes?
[01:21] Diego: right — some generator calls returned truncated tokens due to repeated partial execution; the client retried and we saw duplicate work. also autoscaler decisions were based on a single metric with a short window.
[01:35] Samantha: we saw the latency spikes on our end around 02/15 11:43 UTC and it affected our user flows for about 27 minutes total — which matches your timeline. the big ask from leadership is: what prevents this from happening again, and how will we be alerted earlier?
[01:52] Priya: action items there, we added a new alert for sustained KV eviction errors and another for autoscaler panic. diego will walk through the alert thresholds shortly.
[02:06] Diego: quick note on mitigations: 1) hotfix removes the race by serializing eviction path in the runtime for affected model types, 2) autoscaler backoff now uses a median-smoothed metric with a 2-minute cool-down, 3) we added a circuit breaker for repetitive retries that returns a 503 fast-fail after N retries with diagnostics.
[02:30] Ravi: about the circuit breaker — what's the impact on success rate? we can't have legitimate long requests prematurely failed.
[02:37] Diego: great question. the breaker is configured to look at duplication patterns: only when the same request signature retries X times within Y seconds do we fast-fail. default X is 5 and Y is 20s, we can tune per-customer; we also expose a header so you can correlate. in our tests p99 success didn't change for normal traffic.
[02:58] Nina: are these per-deployment settings? i.e., can we pin different thresholds for our dedicated pool vs hosted?
[03:05] Maya: yes — you can apply policies per-route or per-dedicated-pool. for argosy dedicated plans we'll commit to conservative defaults and then tune after the benchmark.
[03:15] Samantha: legal side: Tom, anything on data retention or audit we should be aware of post-patch?
[03:21] Tom: no new asks right now; we'd like the patch notes and the timeline documented since execs will want to show remediation steps for the customer letter.
[03:31] Maya: will do — we'll include an executive summary and timeline in the postmortem doc.
[03:36] Diego: demo time — quick share: the PR includes logs instrumented at the eviction path and a new telemetry tag "kv_eviction_reason" which should show up in your traces. if you look at the sample trace we sent, you'll see the sequence where retries spiked.
[03:55] Ravi: got it; we'll pull that trace into our observability stack. what's the rollout plan? are we doing canary first?
[04:02] Diego: yes canary ~5% of traffic for 2 hours, then 25% for 4 hours, full rollout if no regression. rollback is a single API flag flip; we've validated rollback within 90s in our lab.
[04:15] Samantha: we want a stricter canary — can we start at 1% for argosy prod and increase slower?
[04:20] Maya: absolutely, we can accommodate that. we'll set the canary to 1% then 5% then 25% with manual checks at each step.
[04:29] Nina: also request that we get real-time slack alerts during the canary to our SRE channel.
[04:33] Priya: we'll configure a temporary integration and update you before the canary goes live.
[04:40] Samantha: ok great. next, monitoring and long-term reliability: what changes are you making to avoid a similar single-point amplification?
[04:48] Diego: longer-term items: 1) add a second metric for autoscaler decisioning (cpu + queue depth), 2) introduce a grace window for eviction counts to avoid transient spikes, 3) scheduled chaos runs that simulate cache corruption and validate fallback paths, 4) better rollout dashboards with per-route failure attribution.
[05:05] Ravi: can you document the exact metrics and thresholds we should watch?
[05:09] Maya: yes we'll publish a monitoring playbook — it will include the new alert names, thresholds, and recommended ownership.
[05:15] Samantha: on the business side, leadership wants a commitment: we need a follow-up meeting to sign-off before we move to Dedicated. can we target next week?
[05:24] Maya: yes we'll propose slots for the week of 3/8.
[05:28] Diego: quick note on testing: for your workload we recommend a 30-min spike test and a realistic token mix test. we'll supply the test harness and a spreadsheet with expected p50/p95/p99 baselines.
[05:42] Nina: please include suggested quantization/throughput profiles; we've seen some quality regressions at lower quant settings.
[05:49] Diego: understood — we'll include our quantization guidance and suggested models.
[05:52] Samantha: any legal implications of the circuit breaker returning 503s? sometimes that triggers SLA clauses.
[05:58] Tom: we'll review the SLA language; if fast-fail behaviour is considered part of mitigation maybe we need an addendum, but first step is to get metrics so we can assess SLA exposure.
[06:10] Maya: we'll put together the SLA impact note and share with you.
[06:14] Priya: circling back to runbook updates — we'll add step-by-step for triage, include the new telemetry fields, and embed the rollback flag location.
[06:24] Samantha: excellent. two quick asks: 1) share the postmortem doc, 2) share the hotfix/patch link, 3) schedule follow-up for 3/8.
[06:33] Maya: will do all three.
[06:35] Diego: tech note — we also recommend a config tweak: increase kv cache reclaim threshold from 70% to 80% for argosy pools to reduce eviction frequency under normal burst patterns. small change but helps.
[06:48] Ravi: ok please add that as a recommended setting in the doc; we'll evaluate.
[06:52] Nina: i also want a list of test cases you'll run for your internal regression suite so we can mirror them.
[06:58] Diego: we'll export the test case list and share.
[07:02] Maya: final recap: action items and owners (we'll put in the ticket): 1) postmortem + exec summary (Maya), 2) hotfix PR + rollout plan (Diego), 3) runbook + alert config (Priya), 4) customer benchmark and results (Ravi).
[07:20] Samantha: thanks everyone, appreciate the fast turnaround. we'll get the benchmark started as soon as we have the patch.
[07:27] Tom: thanks, we'll also loop in procurement for any SLA addendum if needed.
[07:33] Maya: great, we'll follow up by email with the doc links and next meeting invite.
